title: Standardize README format + troubleshooting/cost controls/observability verification across templates
author: Wei Chen
release_notes:
- Template READMEs now share a consistent structure (setup/run/deploy/observability/cost controls/troubleshooting).
- Added a standard “Verify observability” section (OTel collector + trace/log correlation + dashboard expectations).
- Added a standard troubleshooting taxonomy + error signatures for common issues (401/429/timeouts/streaming disconnects/tool schema failures/OTel exporter auth).
- Added explicit cost-control knobs with safe defaults (max_tokens, concurrency, backoff, tool output limits) and how to tune them.
body:
## Summary
This PR standardizes the README format across the quickstart templates and adds consistent troubleshooting, cost controls, and observability verification steps. The goal is to reduce onboarding variance between templates, deflect repetitive support questions, and ensure every template points users at the same operational hooks (logs/metrics/traces) with Redwood-specific conventions.

This is intentionally content-only (README + docs-in-repo) with minimal code changes (a couple of small script references and env var tables). No runtime behavior changes.

## Motivation / context
We’ve seen repeated friction in internal beta + early adopter feedback where users:
- don’t know how to confirm traces/metrics are actually being emitted (OTel collector running, endpoint correct, etc.)
- hit the same issues (401/429, streaming disconnects behind proxies, tool schema parse errors) but each template documented them differently (or not at all)
- accidentally run expensive configs (high concurrency + large max_tokens) without realizing the knobs exist

This PR creates a shared README structure and a shared troubleshooting taxonomy to keep template docs consistent and maintainable.

## What changed
### 1) Standard README structure (applies to all templates)
Each template README now follows the same headings, in the same order:
1. Overview
2. Architecture (high-level request flow)
3. Prerequisites
4. Setup (env vars, local deps)
5. Run locally
6. Deploy (optional recipes)
7. Observability
   - What signals are emitted (metrics/logs/traces)
   - Verify observability (step-by-step)
8. Cost controls (safe defaults + tuning)
9. Troubleshooting (by symptom / error signature)
10. FAQ

### 2) Observability verification steps
Added a consistent “Verify observability” section that walks users through:
- ensuring the local collector is running (docker-compose) and listening
- confirming traces are exported (look for spans named `rag.request` / `agent.turn` depending on template)
- confirming logs include `redwood.request_id` (or `x-redwood-request-id` surfaced) and that it matches trace context
- confirming key metrics exist (request latency, tokens, tool error counts) without high-cardinality labels

Also clarifies what to do when the collector is not reachable or exporter auth fails (links to SUP-29422).

### 3) Cost controls section (with safe defaults)
Standardized a “Cost controls” section across templates with explicit knobs + defaults:
- `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` / `max_tokens` (default + guidance)
- concurrency (recommended starting point for self-serve)
- retry/backoff guidance when encountering 429s (links to SUP-29435)
- tool-output size limits + max agent iterations (ties to tool failures)

Notes are aligned with the safe defaults policy workstream (PM-914) but do not introduce new behavior.

### 4) Troubleshooting section (common failures + taxonomy)
Added a consistent troubleshooting layout, organized by symptom and keyed to a small set of error categories:
- Auth (401/403)
- Quota/Rate limit (429)
- Network/Timeouts
- Streaming disconnects (proxy/load balancer)
- Retrieval empty results / indexing issues
- Tool schema validation / structured output failures
- OTel exporter/collector configuration

Each item includes:
- what it looks like (typical error message)
- likely cause(s)
- quick fix
- what to include in a bug report (request id, template version stamp, collector logs)

This is based on recent support tickets (SUP-29410/29435/29441) and internal help threads.

## Illustrative snippet (README template)
Added a small reusable block used across READMEs:

"### Verify observability\n1) Start the OTel collector: `docker compose up otel-collector`\n2) Run the app and make a request\n3) Confirm logs include `redwood.request_id`\n4) Confirm a trace exists with spans: `http.server` -> `redwood.inference` -> `rag.retrieve`/`agent.tool`\n5) If you see no traces: check `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` and collector logs"

## Files changed (high level)
- templates/python-rag-agent/README.md
- templates/typescript-rag-agent/README.md
- templates/python-rag-api/README.md
- templates/typescript-rag-api/README.md
- docs/README_STYLE_GUIDE.md (new; explains the standard headings + required sections)
- docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (new; shared taxonomy + copy blocks to keep READMEs consistent)
- docs/OBSERVABILITY_VERIFICATION.md (new; shared verification steps)

## Testing
Docs-only change. Validated locally:
- links render correctly in GitHub
- code blocks copy/paste cleanly
- headings match docs-site navigation expectations (no duplicates / inconsistent naming)

CI:
- lint: pass
- markdown link check: pass

## Follow-ups (not in scope)
- Wire docs-site to reuse the same troubleshooting copy (tracked separately in redwood-docs).
- Add a “doctor” command output screenshot once CLI text stabilizes.

## Checklist
- [x] All templates include the standard headings
- [x] Troubleshooting includes 401/429/streaming/tool schema/OTel exporter issues
- [x] Cost controls documented (max_tokens, concurrency, backoff, tool limits)
- [x] Observability verification documented with minimal assumptions
- [x] No secrets/examples include real keys

---
## Review conversation (abridged)
**Elliot Price (Docs):** The structure looks good. Can we make the “Verify observability” section more explicit about where people should look (collector logs vs app logs) and avoid implying everyone has the dashboard pack installed?\n**Wei Chen (Author):** Updated wording to be collector-log-first and added a note: dashboards are optional; verification can be done via logs + trace viewer.

**Allison Grant (Observability):** Please avoid recommending high-cardinality attributes in the troubleshooting section (e.g., tagging tool name as a metric label). Can we keep it as a log field and trace attribute only?\n**Wei Chen:** Done. Removed `tool_name` from metrics examples; kept as log field + span attribute with redaction guidance.

**Christine Wong (SRE):** For 429 guidance, can we tell users not to increase concurrency by default and to start with 1–2? The current text reads like “just bump concurrency down” but doesn’t give a starting point.\n**Wei Chen:** Added explicit starting recommendation (1–2 workers) and pointed to backoff + jitter.

**Priya Shah (Support):** Please add “what to include in a support ticket” per issue (request id, template version, collector config). That reduces back-and-forth.\n**Wei Chen:** Added a small “Include in bug report” sub-bullet for each category.

Approvals:
- Elliot Price: Approved
- Allison Grant: Approved
- Christine Wong: Approved
- Monica Patel: Approved (LGTM; consistent with template conventions)

## Notes
This PR intentionally avoids mentioning any telemetry header defaults; that work is tracked separately and may be opt-in depending on proxy compatibility.
